purpose: Held-out questions for the optional hybrid-retrieval extension. Written and evidence-verified BEFORE any hybrid run. Gold pages are different from the gold pages of the 20 original questions (dev/test). Never used to tune hybrid parameters (those are chosen on the 15 dev questions only).
split_policy: All 10 questions have split='holdout'. They are evaluated only after hybrid parameters are frozen (see starter/results/hybrid/FROZEN.md).
filter_note: Same convention as benchmark.json: filter is an assumed input given before retrieval; C-style runs apply it only to the 3 questions that carry one.

questions.question: Is registration required to obtain protection for a work?
questions.expected_answer: No. Protection is automatic at the moment of creation; registration is only required to file an infringement suit in federal court.
questions.evidence_quote: Interestingly, registration is not required to obtain a copyright.
questions.filter_rationale: Trademark registration (p.157) is also discussed; the filter says the user is in the copyright chapter.

questions.question: Which federal statute created a federal cause of action for trade secret misappropriation, and when was it signed?
questions.expected_answer: The Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA), signed on May 11, 2016.
questions.evidence_quote: on May 11, 2016, the federal Defend Trade Secrets Act (DTSA) was signed into law

questions.question: How is misappropriation defined under the Uniform Trade Secrets Act?
questions.expected_answer: (1) acquisition of a trade secret through improper means, or (2) disclosure or use of a trade secret without consent.
questions.evidence_quote: “Misappropriation” is defined in two ways: (1) acquisition of a trade secret through improper means, or (2) disclosure or use of a trade secret without consent.

questions.question: Which two factors matter most when a court decides whether a defendant's mark is likely to confuse consumers?
questions.expected_answer: The similarity in the overall impression created by the two marks, and the similarities of the goods and services involved.
questions.evidence_quote: The two most important are: • The similarity in the overall impression created by the two marks (including the marks’ look, phonetic similarities, and underlying meanings) • The similarities of the goods and services involved.

questions.question: How does a collective membership mark differ from a collective trademark or service mark?
questions.expected_answer: A collective membership mark shows that a person belongs to an organization (e.g. a trade union or Rotary Club) and is not used to identify the source of goods or services, whereas a collective trade or service mark indicates the source of goods or services of the group's members.
questions.evidence_quote: A collective membership mark, by contrast, is used to indicate that a person is a member of some organization, such as a trade union or an association like the Rotary Club, but is not used to identify the source of goods and services.

questions.question: Why do owners almost invariably insist on an injunction rather than only money?
questions.expected_answer: Because the biggest loss from infringement is not necessarily revenue but damage to the brand's reputation in the minds of consumers.
questions.evidence_quote: trademark owners almost invariably insist on injunctive (e.g. prohibiting continued sales) to cure the infringement.
questions.filter_rationale: Patent (p.89-90) and trade secret (p.185) chapters also discuss injunctions.

questions.question: How long do lawsuits typically take to reach trial?
questions.expected_answer: Two to four years (post-trial proceedings can add six months to a year, and appeals several more years).
questions.evidence_quote: Lawsuits typically take two to four years to reach trial.

questions.question: If I release my video under a Creative Commons license, can I later take it back from everyone who copied it?
questions.expected_answer: No. Creative Commons licenses cannot be revoked; copies distributed under the license will always be distributed that way.
questions.evidence_quote: Creative Commons licenses also cannot be revoked, which means that if copies of your work are distributed under a Creative Commons license, they will always be distributed that way.
questions.leakage_risk: Deliberate vocabulary gap: question says 'take it back', source says 'revoked'. May favor dense over keyword matching.

questions.question: Can a product that does not actually work, like snake oil, meet the utility requirement for a patent?
questions.expected_answer: No. Snake oil medicines and other products that do not work in any meaningful way will not meet the utility requirement.
questions.evidence_quote: snake oil medicines and other products that do not work in any meaningful way will not meet the requirement for utility.
questions.leakage_risk: Distinctive keywords ('snake oil'); may favor keyword matching.

questions.question: How much can punitive damages exceed the damage award, and can the cap change?
questions.expected_answer: A punitive or exemplary award may not exceed twice the damage award, but some states have modified this cap.
questions.evidence_quote: A punitive or exemplary award may not exceed twice the amount of the damage award.
questions.filter_rationale: Patent (treble damages, p.70) and copyright remedies also involve enhanced damages.
